comment: gorilla/mux 1.8 on Go 1.27, one function per family registering its routes in the implementation package under Implementation/, and the server's main package in container-h1. The suite is UnitTests/, go test over the router served by net/http/httptest, and never reaches the image. mux is a router over net/http and binds nothing, so each family uses the gorilla toolkit where it has something (handlers for CORS, compression and recovery, schema for query strings and forms), net/http where it does not, and code written for the family where neither does. Bodies are decoded with encoding/json and checked with go-playground's validator, and a refusal is 400 with the error's text under error, written with encoding/json's encoder as mux's README writes JSON. The first-error route is wired by hand, because go-playground cannot stop at the first failure. cors.vary is skipped because gorilla/handlers writes Vary: Origin only for a policy of more than one origin. The lockfile is go.mod, which records every module version the build selects, and go.sum, which holds their hashes. upgrade is go get -u ./..., which moves every module to its newest release within its major version.

skips.cors.vary: gorilla/handlers' CORS writes Vary: Origin only when the policy allows more than one origin, and settings.json names one.

noHandler.cors.preflight: gorilla/handlers' CORS middleware on the /cors subrouter answers the preflight, on a route that names OPTIONS so the subrouter runs its middlewares.
noHandler.errors.unmatched: mux answers a path no route matches with net/http's NotFoundHandler, a 404 with a text body.
noHandler.errors.wrong_method: mux answers a method the path has no route for with its own 405, which writes no body and no Allow header.

authorized.mechanism: A middleware on the /authorized subrouter that compares the bearer token and refuses any other with http.Error and 403, as mux's README writes its authentication middleware

baseline.builtin: The handler writes the text with io.WriteString after setting text/plain.

body.mechanism: encoding/json decodes the order, and on the validate routes go-playground's validator checks the validate tags. The first-error route runs the same validator over one field at a time, because go-playground cannot stop at the first failure

cache.mechanism: A middleware on a subrouter in front of each cache route that replays a stored answer and otherwise stores what the handler wrote, keyed by the path and the route's vary headers, one store per process

compressed.mechanism: gorilla/handlers' CompressHandlerLevel on the /compressed subrouter, at gzip's fastest level

cors.mechanism: gorilla/handlers' CORS middleware on the /cors subrouter, with OPTIONS named on the route so a preflight reaches it

errors.builtin: mux answers a miss with net/http's 404 text, and a method a path lacks with a bare 405. A body the decoder cannot read is refused with 400 and the decoder's message, and the items handlers answer a missing row with net/http's NotFound.

etag.mechanism: A middleware on the /etag subrouter that holds back the body, hashes it with SHA-1 and answers a matching If-None-Match with 304

forms.builtin: net/http parses the two bodies and gorilla/schema decodes their values into structs, converting the numbers, as schema's README decodes a form.

headers.builtin: The three headers are read from net/http's header map, the account converted with strconv.

items.builtin: One route per method on /items/{id}, the id read with mux.Vars. The read route names GET and HEAD, because mux answers HEAD only where a route names it.

json.builtin: encoding/json's encoder writes the payload after the handler sets application/json.

middleware.mechanism: No-op mux.MiddlewareFunc layers on a subrouter of the route's own path, which mux wraps around the matched handler on every request, four or sixteen of them

parameters.builtin: mux.Vars reads each capture as a string, which strconv converts.

query.builtin: gorilla/schema decodes the query string into a struct, converting the numbers.

sse.builtin: Written by hand, because mux and the gorilla toolkit have no event stream. Each row is one event, flushed through net/http's ResponseController.

static.builtin: A path prefix hands each file to net/http's FileServer, exactly as mux's README serves static files.

stream.builtin: encoding/json's encoder writes each row and its newline, flushed through net/http's ResponseController.

template.mechanism: html/template, embedded in the binary and parsed once, executed into the response by the handler, because mux has no view layer
